topic: Barycentric displaced micro-mesh (DMM) analytical intersection vs POM ray-march ridge tunneling rig
topic_zh: 二进重心位移微网格（DMM）闭式求交对比固定步长 POM 视差步进穿峰漏检
scope: Deterministic dyadic barycentric micro-mesh (DMM) tessellation and closed-form ray-segment intersection versus coarse fixed-step Parallax Occlusion Mapping (POM) ray-marching across 17 grazing silhouette rays. No neural displacement synthesis executed.

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating Node CPU runs after warmup. Closed-form linear ray-microsegment intersection versus 48-step binary bisection root-finding baseline.

protocol.function: t* = (y_ray − H_k)/(H_{k+1} − H_k) on 2^L dyadic lattice → 0 tunneled rays (vs 9/17 POM misses)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 grazing silhouette rays intersect the watertight barycentric micro-mesh with zero ridge tunneling

good_fit: Hardware/compute-shader Displaced Micro-Meshes (DMM), Nanite-style micro-polygon displacement, and ray-traced terrain/masonry silhouettes
Explaining why fixed-step Parallax Occlusion Mapping (POM) tunnels through narrow ridges and slices grazing silhouettes into pancakes
Using a regular 2^L dyadic barycentric grid so micro-vertices are addressed implicitly without storing index buffers
Solving ray-microsegment intersection in O(1) via t* = (y_ray - H_k) / (H_{k+1} - H_k) without iterative secant/bisection steps
not_for: Flat painted surfaces with zero geometric relief where standard normal mapping suffices
Overhanging 3D caves or vector-displaced earlobes that fold back over the base triangle normal (requires 3D mesh or vector displacement)
Distant low-LOD background props smaller than 1 screen pixel
